title: S1 pulse-shape discrimination at 550 phd: what singlet/triplet ratios, photon statistics and propagation in a 1.5 m TPC allow, and why LZ called it inconclusive
question: What ER/NR discrimination does a 540 phd S1 carry under recalled singlet/triplet brackets once photon propagation in the 1.5 m LZ TPC, PMT jitter and 10 ns sampling are included; what does LZ's statement that 150 keV AmBe NRs match an ER template imply about the intrinsic ER-NR timing difference and the best single-event likelihood ratio; how strong is the RFR-vs-FV depth argument?
headline_result: Recalled brackets predict 1.4-8 sigma ER/NR separation at 540 phd (bracket centre 4.5 sigma ideal, 3.4 sigma prompt fraction) even after a 29 ns propagation spread that halves the point-detector separation; LZ's 'AmBe 150 keV not inconsistent with ER template' therefore bounds the ER-NR mean-emission-time difference to <~2 ns and any single-event PSD LR to <~2-5, while RFR-vs-event-depth origin is separated at 6-8 sigma in rise time, prompt fraction and TBA
key_numbers: propagation at z=26.4 cm: mean 27 ns, sd 29 ns, f_top 0.21, TBA -0.58 (RFR -0.84); separation 8.7->4.5 sigma with propagation; bracket centre d=3.4 (fp20)/3.7 (tmean)/4.5 (ideal) at 540 phd, 2.7/2.9/3.4 at 297 phd; closest pair 1.4 sigma, LR 3.1; d(540)=0.6 sigma per ns; AmBe bound n=5/10/30: Delta<2.0/1.5/1.0 ns, d(540)<1.2/0.85/0.44, LR<2.1/1.4/1.1; position shift +8.4 ns (26->100 cm), +-5 cm residual 0.7 sigma; RFR vs FV: rise 16.1 vs 25.6 ns (6.2 sigma), fp 0.49 vs 0.31 (7.1 sigma), TBA 7.6 sigma
model_or_mechanism: toy S1 waveform: singlet/triplet(/recombination) exponential mixture + optical photon MC (cylinder, PTFE Lambertian R=0.95, Rayleigh 35 cm, TIR at surface, grids, arrays; tuned to g1=0.110) + 1.5 ns TTS + 10 ns digitisation; statistics f_p(20 ns), mean time, ideal position-matched template LR profiled over t0; singlet-fraction scan; Gaussian LR conversions
